source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־תִּמְצָ֖א אֱכ֑וֹל אֱכוֹל֙ אֶת־הַמְּגִלָּ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את וְלֵ֥ךְ דַּבֵּ֖ר אֶל־בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to me, Son of man, what you find, eat; eat the scroll this, and go, speak to [the] house of Israel.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Son of man, what you find, eat. Eat this scroll, and go [and] speak to the house of Israel."
en.B: He said to me, "Son of man, eat what is in front of you. Eat this scroll, and then go and speak to the house of Israel."
en.R: He said to me, "Son of man, eat what you see in front of you. Eat this scroll. Then go and speak to the people of Israel."

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me disse: "Filho do homem, o que encontrares, come. Come este rolo, e vai, fala à casa de Israel."
pt.B: Ele me disse: "Filho do homem, come o que está diante de ti. Come este rolo, e depois vai e fala à casa de Israel."
pt.R: Ele me disse: "Filho do homem, come o que estás vendo na tua frente. Come este rolo. Depois vai e fala ao povo de Israel."

decisions.choice: eat this scroll, and go, speak: the message must become his own before he speaks it
decisions.reason: Eating the scroll is a sign of taking God's word wholly into oneself. Ezekiel is not to make up his message, nor only to repeat it, but to take it in and then speak it (verse 4: "speak with my words"). Jeremiah uses the same picture (Jeremiah 15:16), and Revelation 10:9-10 takes it up (see verse 3).

decisions.choice: what you find, eat: eat what is before you
decisions.reason: The phrase means "eat what is there", what has been set before him, and the next words say what that is: this scroll.

decisions.choice: the people of Israel (R)
decisions.reason: "The house of Israel" is kept at Literal and Balanced; Readable says "the people of Israel", which is what the phrase means, as in Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: a casa de Israel (L, B); o povo de Israel (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as the English (r-en-1) and the shared rules for Ezekiel: "a casa de Israel" at Literal and Balanced, the phrase Portuguese readers know from the prophets; Readable says what it means, "o povo de Israel", as Jeremiah's Readable does.

source.text: וָאֶפְתַּ֖ח אֶת־פִּ֑י וַיַּ֣אֲכִלֵ֔נִי אֵ֖ת הַמְּגִלָּ֥ה הַזֹּֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: And I opened my mouth, and he made me eat the scroll this.

en.L: And I opened my mouth, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made me eat this scroll.
en.B: So I opened my mouth, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave me the scroll to eat.
en.R: So I opened my mouth, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} fed me the scroll.

pt.L: E abri a minha boca, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me fez comer este rolo.
pt.B: Então abri a boca, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me deu o rolo para comer.
pt.R: Então abri a boca, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me alimentou com o rolo.

decisions.choice: he made me eat: the LORD feeds him
decisions.reason: The verb is causative: Ezekiel opens his mouth, and the LORD feeds him the scroll. The message is given to the prophet; he does not take it for himself.

decisions.choice: gave me the scroll to eat (B); fed me (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "gave me ... to eat" and "fed me" for the causative verb (m1).

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י בֶּן־אָדָם֙ בִּטְנְךָ֤ תַֽאֲכֵל֙ וּמֵעֶ֣יךָ תְמַלֵּ֔א אֵ֚ת הַמְּגִלָּ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י נֹתֵ֣ן אֵלֶ֑יךָ וָאֹ֣כְלָ֔ה וַתְּהִ֥י בְּפִ֖י כִּדְבַ֥שׁ לְמָתֽוֹק׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And he said to me, Son of man, your belly feed and your inner parts fill with the scroll this which I [am] giving to you. And I ate [it], and it was in my mouth like honey for sweetness.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Son of man, feed your belly and fill your stomach with this scroll that I am giving you." And I ate [it], and it was in my mouth like honey for sweetness.
en.B: He said to me, "Son of man, eat this scroll I am giving you and fill your stomach with it." So I ate it, and in my mouth it tasted as sweet as honey.
en.R: He said to me, "Son of man, eat this scroll that I am giving you. Fill your stomach with it." So I ate it, and it tasted as sweet as honey.

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me disse: "Filho do homem, alimenta o teu ventre e enche as tuas entranhas com este rolo que eu te dou." E [o] comi, e ele foi na minha boca como mel em doçura.
pt.B: Ele me disse: "Filho do homem, come este rolo que eu te dou e enche o teu estômago com ele." Então eu o comi, e na minha boca ele foi doce como mel.
pt.R: Ele me disse: "Filho do homem, come este rolo que eu estou te dando. Enche o teu estômago com ele." Então eu o comi, e ele tinha o gosto doce do mel.

decisions.choice: the scroll sweet as honey: Revelation 10:9-10
decisions.reason: John is told to take the little scroll from the angel and eat it: "in your mouth it will be sweet as honey", but it will make his stomach bitter (Revelation 10:9-10). Revelation takes up Ezekiel's scene and adds the bitterness. In Ezekiel the bitterness comes afterward, in his own spirit (verse 14).

decisions.choice: sweet as honey: God's word is sweet even when it brings grief
decisions.reason: The scroll is full of laments and woe (2:10), and yet it is sweet. The sweetness belongs to the word as God's word, as the psalms say: "sweeter than honey" (Psalm 19:11; 119:103). Ezekiel finds joy in receiving it, whatever its message.

decisions.choice: your belly and your inner parts: take it in completely
decisions.reason: The two words for the inside of the body say that the scroll is to fill him, not stay in his mouth. The word for "inner parts" is used of the seat of feeling too.

decisions.choice: eat this scroll ... and fill your stomach with it (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the two parallel commands, "feed your belly and fill your stomach". Balanced and Readable put them into one plain command, "eat ... and fill your stomach". Balanced and Readable say "as sweet as honey" for "like honey for sweetness".

decisions.choice: como mel em doçura (L); doce como mel (B); o gosto doce do mel (R)
decisions.reason: Revelation 10:9-10 takes up this scene (m1), so Balanced and Readable use the words John's scroll has there in Portuguese, "na minha boca ... doce como mel" (Balanced) and "o gosto doce do mel" (Readable), and the scroll is "o rolo" in both books. Literal keeps the Hebrew "like honey for sweetness".

source.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑י בֶּן־אָדָ֗ם לֶךְ־בֹּא֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְדִבַּרְתָּ֥ בִדְבָרַ֖י אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to me, Son of man, go, enter to [the] house of Israel, and speak with my words to them.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Son of man, go, get yourself to the house of Israel, and speak with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words to them.
en.B: He said to me, "Son of man, set out now for the house of Israel and speak {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words to them.
en.R: He said to me, "Son of man, go to the people of Israel and tell them what I say.

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me disse: "Filho do homem, vai, dirige-te à casa de Israel, e fala a eles com as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} palavras.
pt.B: Ele me disse: "Filho do homem, põe-te a caminho agora para a casa de Israel e fala a eles as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} palavras.
pt.R: Ele me disse: "Filho do homem, vai até o povo de Israel e conta a eles o que eu digo.

decisions.choice: speak with my words to them: with God's words, not his own
decisions.reason: The two verbs "go, enter" urge him on his way. He is to speak "with my words": the words of the scroll he has eaten. The speech that begins here runs to the end of verse 9.

decisions.choice: go, get yourself to (L); set out now (B)
decisions.reason: The two verbs, "go" and "come" or "enter", together mean "go at once". Literal keeps two verbs; Balanced says "go now"; Readable says "go". Readable says "what I say" for "my words", as in 2:7.

source.text: כִּ֡י לֹא֩ אֶל־עַ֨ם עִמְקֵ֥י שָׂפָ֛ה וְכִבְדֵ֥י לָשׁ֖וֹן אַתָּ֣ה שָׁל֑וּחַ אֶל־בֵּ֖ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: For not to a people deep of lip and heavy of tongue [are] you sent, to [the] house of Israel,

en.L: For not to a people deep of lip and heavy of tongue are you sent, [but] to the house of Israel,
en.B: You are not being sent to a people of obscure speech and difficult language, but to the house of Israel,
en.R: I am not sending you to people whose language is strange and hard to understand. I am sending you to the people of Israel.

pt.L: Pois não a um povo de lábio profundo e de língua pesada tu és enviado, [mas] à casa de Israel,
pt.B: Tu não estás sendo enviado a um povo de fala obscura e de língua difícil, mas à casa de Israel,
pt.R: Eu não estou te enviando a um povo cuja língua é estranha e difícil de entender. Eu te envio ao povo de Israel.

decisions.choice: deep of lip and heavy of tongue: speaking a foreign language that is hard to understand
decisions.reason: A "deep" lip is speech that cannot be fathomed; a "heavy" tongue is one that is hard to follow. Isaiah speaks of the Assyrians as a people "of a speech too deep to understand, of a stammering tongue" (Isaiah 33:19). Ezekiel's hearers speak his own language, so they cannot say that they did not understand.

decisions.choice: of obscure speech and difficult language (B); whose language is strange and hard to understand (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the two pictures. Balanced and Readable say what they mean (m1). Literal brackets "but", which the sense requires.

source.text: לֹ֣א׀אֶל־עַמִּ֣ים רַבִּ֗ים עִמְקֵ֤י שָׂפָה֙ וְכִבְדֵ֣י לָשׁ֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־תִשְׁמַ֖ע דִּבְרֵיהֶ֑ם אִם־לֹ֤א אֲלֵיהֶם֙ שְׁלַחְתִּ֔יךָ הֵ֖מָּה יִשְׁמְע֥וּ אֵלֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: not to peoples many deep of lip and heavy of tongue whose words you will not understand; if not to them I sent you, they would listen to you.

en.L: not to many peoples deep of lip and heavy of tongue, whose words you cannot understand. Surely, had I sent you to them, they would listen to you.
en.B: not to many peoples of obscure speech and difficult language, whose words you cannot understand. Surely, had I sent you to them, they would have listened to you.
en.R: I am not sending you to many nations that speak strange, hard languages you cannot understand. If I had sent you to them, they would surely have listened to you.

pt.L: não a muitos povos de lábio profundo e de língua pesada, cujas palavras não podes entender. Certamente, se eu te enviasse a eles, eles te ouviriam.
pt.B: não a muitos povos de fala obscura e de língua difícil, cujas palavras não consegues entender. Certamente, se eu te tivesse enviado a eles, eles te teriam escutado.
pt.R: Não estou te enviando a muitas nações que falam línguas estranhas e difíceis, que não consegues entender. Se eu te tivesse enviado a elas, com certeza elas teriam te escutado.

decisions.choice: if I had sent you to them, they would listen to you: the foreigners would have listened
decisions.reason: The two small words at the start of the clause can mean "if not" or work as an oath, "surely". Read as an oath, the line says that foreign peoples would have listened, unlike Israel (verse 7). Some read it as a plain condition: "but if I sent you to them", with the same sense.

decisions.choice: they would listen to you: foreigners who listen
decisions.reason: The book of Jonah tells how the people of Nineveh, a foreign city, listened to a prophet and turned from their ways (Jonah 3:5-10). Jesus makes the same contrast between the cities of Galilee and Tyre and Sidon (Matthew 11:21) and Nineveh (Matthew 12:41).

decisions.choice: would have listened (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the result in the past, "would have listened", to match "if I had sent you". Literal keeps "would listen".

source.text: וּבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לֹ֤א יֹאבוּ֙ לִשְׁמֹ֣עַ אֵלֶ֔יךָ כִּֽי־אֵינָ֥ם אֹבִ֖ים לִשְׁמֹ֣עַ אֵלָ֑י כִּ֚י כָּל־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל חִזְקֵי־מֵ֥צַח וּקְשֵׁי־לֵ֖ב הֵֽמָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] house of Israel will not be willing to listen to you, for they [are] not willing to listen to me; for all [the] house of Israel [are] strong of forehead and hard of heart they.

en.L: But the house of Israel will not be willing to listen to you, for they are not willing to listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; for all the house of Israel [are] hard of forehead and stubborn of heart.
en.B: But the house of Israel will refuse to listen to you, because they refuse to listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. The whole house of Israel is hard-headed and stubborn.
en.R: But the people of Israel will refuse to listen to you, because they refuse to listen to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. All of them are hard-headed and stubborn.

pt.L: Mas a casa de Israel não quererá te ouvir, pois não querem {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ouvir; porque toda a casa de Israel [é] dura de testa e obstinada de coração.
pt.B: Mas a casa de Israel vai se recusar a te ouvir, porque se recusa a {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ouvir. Toda a casa de Israel é cabeça-dura e obstinada.
pt.R: Mas o povo de Israel vai se recusar a te ouvir, porque se recusa a {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ouvir. Todos eles são cabeças-duras e teimosos.

decisions.choice: not willing to listen to you, for not willing to listen to me: refusing the prophet is refusing God
decisions.reason: Their refusal is not aimed at Ezekiel himself. The LORD said the same to Samuel when the people asked for a king (1 Samuel 8:7), and Jesus to his disciples (Luke 10:16).

decisions.choice: hard of forehead and stubborn of heart: brazen and obstinate
decisions.reason: A hard forehead is one that will not bow or blush; Isaiah 48:4 says that Israel's forehead is bronze. The word for "hard" here is the root of Ezekiel's name ("God strengthens"); see verses 8-9.

decisions.choice: will refuse to listen (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Will not be willing to listen" is kept at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "refuse to listen". "Hard-headed" at Balanced and Readable is the English picture for a hard forehead.

source.text: הִנֵּ֨ה נָתַ֧תִּי אֶת־פָּנֶ֛יךָ חֲזָקִ֖ים לְעֻמַּ֣ת פְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וְאֶֽת־מִצְחֲךָ֥ חָזָ֖ק לְעֻמַּ֥ת מִצְחָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: See, I have made your face hard against their faces, and your forehead hard against their forehead.

en.L: See, I have made your face hard to match their faces, and your forehead hard to match their foreheads.
en.B: But I have made your face as hard as theirs, and your forehead as firm as their foreheads.
en.R: But I have made you just as hard and determined as they are.

pt.L: Eis que fiz o teu rosto duro à altura dos seus rostos, e a tua testa dura à altura das suas testas.
pt.B: Mas eu fiz o teu rosto tão duro quanto o deles, e a tua testa tão firme quanto a deles.
pt.R: Mas eu te fiz tão duro e firme quanto eles.

decisions.choice: hard: the root of Ezekiel's name
decisions.reason: The word for "hard", strong or firm, is the root of the name Ezekiel, "God strengthens" (see 1:3). The hard people of verse 7 will meet a prophet made hard by God: the name is fulfilled in his calling. Jeremiah is made "a fortified city, an iron pillar and bronze walls" in the same way (Jeremiah 1:18), and the servant in Isaiah 50:7 sets his face like flint.

decisions.choice: as hard as (B); just as hard and determined as they are (R)
decisions.reason: The small word here means "against" in the sense of "to match", which Literal says. Balanced says "as hard as". Readable says what the hard face and forehead stand for: firmness that will not give way. Balanced and Readable begin with "But" for the pointing word, traditionally "behold", which here turns from the people to Ezekiel.

source.text: כְּשָׁמִ֛יר חָזָ֥ק מִצֹּ֖ר נָתַ֣תִּי מִצְחֶ֑ךָ לֹֽא־תִירָ֤א אוֹתָם֙ וְלֹא־תֵחַ֣ת מִפְּנֵיהֶ֔ם כִּ֛י בֵּֽית־מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Like diamond harder than flint I have made your forehead; do not fear them and do not be dismayed at their faces, for a house of rebellion [are] they.

en.L: Like diamond, harder than flint, I have made your forehead. Do not fear them, and do not be dismayed before their faces, for they [are] a house of rebellion."
en.B: I have made your forehead like diamond, harder than flint. Do not be afraid of them or terrified by their looks, for they are a rebellious house."
en.R: I have made your forehead as hard as diamond, harder than flint. So do not be afraid of them or frightened by the way they look at you. They are people who refuse to obey."

pt.L: Como diamante, mais duro que a pederneira, fiz a tua testa. Não os temas, e não te assustes diante dos seus rostos, pois eles [são] uma casa de rebelião."
pt.B: Fiz a tua testa como diamante, mais dura que a pederneira. Não tenhas medo deles nem te apavores com os seus olhares, pois são uma casa rebelde."
pt.R: Eu fiz a tua testa dura como diamante, mais dura que a pederneira. Por isso, não tenhas medo deles nem te assustes com o jeito como olham para ti. Eles são um povo que se recusa a obedecer."

decisions.choice: diamond: a very hard stone
decisions.reason: The word names the hardest stone known, used for the engraving point in Jeremiah 17:1 and for the people's hard hearts in Zechariah 7:12. It may have been emery or corundum rather than diamond, but it was harder than flint, the hardest common stone. The wording follows Jeremiah 17:1.

decisions.choice: a house of rebellion / a rebellious house / people who refuse to obey
decisions.reason: The wording set at 2:5. The quotation mark closes the speech begun in verse 4.

source.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑י בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם אֶת־כָּל־דְּבָרַי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֲדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלֶ֔יךָ קַ֥ח בִּֽלְבָבְךָ֖ וּבְאָזְנֶ֥יךָ שְׁמָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to me, Son of man, all my words which I will speak to you, take in your heart and with your ears hear.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Son of man, all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words that I speak to you, take into your heart and hear with your ears.
en.B: He said to me, "Son of man, take to heart all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words that I speak to you, and listen closely.
en.R: He said to me, "Son of man, listen carefully to everything I tell you, and keep it in your heart.

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me disse: "Filho do homem, todas as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} palavras que eu te falar, recebe-as no teu coração e ouve-as com os teus ouvidos.
pt.B: Ele me disse: "Filho do homem, guarda no coração todas as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} palavras que eu te disser, e escuta com atenção.
pt.R: Ele me disse: "Filho do homem, escuta com atenção tudo o que eu te disser e guarda isso no teu coração.

decisions.choice: take into your heart and hear with your ears: receive the words fully
decisions.reason: The heart is the center of thought and will. To "take into the heart" is to accept and remember, and to "hear with the ears" is to listen with full attention. The heart comes first, as if the words must be received before they are even heard: Ezekiel has already eaten the scroll.

decisions.choice: take to heart ... and listen closely (B); listen carefully ... and keep it in your heart (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the order, heart first, and says "listen closely" for "hear with your ears". Readable puts the listening first, as English would. The speech runs on into verse 11.

source.text: וְלֵ֨ךְ בֹּ֤א אֶל־הַגּוֹלָה֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י עַמֶּ֔ךָ וְדִבַּרְתָּ֤ אֲלֵיהֶם֙ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֑ה אִֽם־יִשְׁמְע֖וּ וְאִם־יֶחְדָּֽלוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And go, enter to the exiles, to [the] sons of your people, and speak to them and say to them, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh, whether they will hear or whether they will refrain.

en.L: And go, get yourself to the exiles, to the {{gender:children|sons}} of your people, and speak to them and say to them, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, whether they hear or refrain."
en.B: Go now to the exiles, to your own people, and speak to them. Say to them, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this, whether they listen or refuse."
en.R: Now go to the exiles, your own people. Speak to them. Say to them, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says. Do this whether they listen or not."

pt.L: E vai, dirige-te aos exilados, aos filhos do teu povo, e fala com eles e dize-lhes: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}, quer ouçam, quer deixem de ouvir."
pt.B: Vai agora aos exilados, ao teu próprio povo, e fala com eles. Dize-lhes: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}, quer escutem, quer se recusem."
pt.R: Agora vai até os exilados, o teu próprio povo. Fala com eles. Diz a eles: É isto que o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} diz. Faz isso, quer escutem, quer não."

decisions.choice: the exiles, the children of your people: the Judeans in Babylon
decisions.reason: The exiles are those taken to Babylon with King Jehoiachin in 597 BC (1:2), Ezekiel among them. They are his own people, and his first hearers. Jerusalem has not yet fallen, and many of them expected to go home soon (Jeremiah 29:1-9).

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD / The Lord GOD says this / This is what the Lord GOD says; whether they hear or refrain / listen or refuse / listen or not
decisions.reason: The formulas as set at 2:4 and 2:5. Balanced and Readable say "your own people" for "the children of your people"; Literal gives "children" through the gender setting, since the word means the people as a whole.

decisions.choice: os filhos do teu povo, no gender setting
alternatives: {{gender:os filhos|os filhos homens}} do teu povo
decisions.reason: As at 2:4: Portuguese "filhos" already includes daughters, so Literal needs no gender setting where the English Literal has one; Balanced and Readable say "o teu próprio povo", as the English does.

source.text: וַתִּשָּׂאֵ֣נִי ר֔וּחַ וָאֶשְׁמַ֣ע אַחֲרַ֔י ק֖וֹל רַ֣עַשׁ גָּד֑וֹל בָּר֥וּךְ כְּבוֹד־יְהוָ֖ה מִמְּקוֹמֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And lifted me up a spirit, and I heard behind me a sound of a rumbling great: Blessed [be the] glory of Yahweh from its place.

en.L: And [the] Spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me the sound of a great rumbling: "Blessed [be] the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from its place!"
en.B: Then the Spirit lifted me up, and behind me I heard a great rumbling sound: "Blessed be the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from its place!"
en.R: Then the Spirit lifted me up. Behind me I heard a loud rumbling sound: "Praise the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from the place where it is!"

pt.L: E [o] Espírito me levantou, e ouvi atrás de mim o som de um grande estrondo: "Bendita [seja] a glória {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} desde o seu lugar!"
pt.B: Então o Espírito me levantou, e atrás de mim ouvi o som de um grande estrondo: "Bendita seja a glória {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} desde o seu lugar!"
pt.R: Então o Espírito me levantou. Atrás de mim ouvi um barulho forte, como um estrondo: "Louvada seja a glória {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} no lugar onde ela está!"

decisions.choice: Blessed be the glory of the LORD from its place: the text as it stands
alternatives: as the glory of the LORD rose from its place
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has a cry of praise, "Blessed be the glory of the LORD from its place", heard in the noise of the vision. It is unusual in form, and the speaker is not named. A change of one letter, which some propose, gives "as the glory of the LORD rose from its place", which fits the sound of the wings in verse 13 and the glory's rising in 10:4 and 10:18-19. The text as it stands is followed here.

decisions.choice: a great rumbling: the roar of the moving vision
decisions.reason: The word is used for an earthquake and for the thunder of chariots (Jeremiah 47:3; Nahum 3:2). Verse 13 says what made it: the wings and the wheels.

decisions.choice: the Spirit: as in 2:2
decisions.reason: The Spirit that set Ezekiel on his feet now lifts him up and carries him (verse 14), as in 8:3 and 11:1, 24. See the note at 2:2.

decisions.choice: Praise ... (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "Praise" for "Blessed be", the plain meaning of the cry. Every level capitalizes "Spirit", as at 2:2. Literal and Balanced say "its place": the place of the glory.

source.text: וְק֣וֹל׀כַּנְפֵ֣י הַחַיּ֗וֹת מַשִּׁיקוֹת֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה אֶל־אֲחוֹתָ֔הּ וְק֥וֹל הָאוֹפַנִּ֖ים לְעֻמָּתָ֑ם וְק֖וֹל רַ֥עַשׁ גָּדֽוֹל׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sound of [the] wings of the living creatures touching a woman to her sister, and [the] sound of the wheels close to them, and [the] sound of a rumbling great.

en.L: And [it was] the sound of the wings of the living creatures touching one another, and the sound of the wheels beside them, and the sound of a great rumbling.
en.B: It was the sound of the living creatures' wings brushing against one another, and of the wheels beside them: a great rumbling sound.
en.R: It was the noise of the living creatures' wings touching one another, and the noise of the wheels beside them. It was a loud rumbling sound.

pt.L: E [era] o som das asas dos seres viventes tocando uma na outra, e o som das rodas junto deles, e o som de um grande estrondo.
pt.B: Era o som das asas dos seres viventes roçando umas nas outras, e das rodas ao lado deles: um grande estrondo.
pt.R: Era o barulho das asas dos seres viventes tocando umas nas outras e o barulho das rodas ao lado deles. Era um barulho forte, como um estrondo.

decisions.choice: the sound of the wings ... the sound of the wheels: what made the rumbling
decisions.reason: The verse names the sources of the sound in verse 12, as in 1:24. The verb for "touching" is the one for kissing: the wings brushed against each other. "One another" is the idiom of 1:9, "a woman to her sister".

decisions.choice: brushing against (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "brushing against" for the light touch the verb pictures (m1).

source.text: וְר֥וּחַ נְשָׂאַ֖תְנִי וַתִּקָּחֵ֑נִי וָאֵלֵ֥ךְ מַר֙ בַּחֲמַ֣ת רוּחִ֔י וְיַד־יְהוָ֥ה עָלַ֖י חָזָֽקָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And a spirit lifted me up and took me, and I went bitter in [the] heat of my spirit, and [the] hand of Yahweh on me [was] strong.

en.L: And [the] Spirit lifted me up and took me, and I went bitter in the heat of my spirit, and the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was strong upon me.
en.B: The Spirit lifted me up and carried me off, and I went in bitterness and in the heat of my spirit, with the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} pressing hard on me.
en.R: The Spirit lifted me up and carried me away. I went feeling bitter and angry, and the power of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was strong on me.

pt.L: E [o] Espírito me levantou e me levou, e eu fui amargurado, no ardor do meu espírito, e a mão {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} estava forte sobre mim.
pt.B: O Espírito me levantou e me levou embora, e eu fui com amargura e com o espírito inflamado, com a mão {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} pesando forte sobre mim.
pt.R: O Espírito me levantou e me levou embora. Eu fui amargurado e com raiva, e o poder {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} era forte sobre mim.

decisions.choice: bitter in the heat of my spirit: Ezekiel's own bitterness and anger
decisions.reason: The heat of the spirit is anger. The verse does not say at what Ezekiel was bitter and angry. It may be that he shared the LORD's anger at the people's rebellion, as Jeremiah says he was full of the LORD's wrath (Jeremiah 6:11); or that he was bitter at the hard task laid on him. The sweetness of the scroll in his mouth (verse 3) is followed by bitterness, as in Revelation 10:10.

decisions.choice: the hand of the LORD was strong upon me: the LORD's power overwhelmed him
decisions.reason: The phrase of 1:3, with the verb "to be strong", the root of Ezekiel's name (verse 8). The LORD's power held him firmly; Isaiah 8:11 speaks of the LORD's strong hand on the prophet.

decisions.choice: the hand of the LORD was strong upon me (L); pressing hard on me (B); the power of the LORD was strong on me (R)
decisions.reason: The wording for "the hand of the LORD" (1:3), with "strong" for the verb added here. "Spirit" is capitalized for God's Spirit at the start of the verse and lowercase for Ezekiel's own spirit.

source.text: וָאָב֨וֹא אֶל־הַגּוֹלָ֜ה תֵּ֣ל אָ֠בִיב הַיֹּשְׁבִ֤ים אֶֽל־נְהַר־כְּבָר֙ וָֽאֵשֵׁ֔ב הֵ֖מָּה יוֹשְׁבִ֣ים שָׁ֑ם וָאֵשֵׁ֥ב שָׁ֛ם שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים מַשְׁמִ֥ים בְּתוֹכָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I came to the exiles [at] Tel-abib who were dwelling by [the] river Kebar, and I sat where they were dwelling there, and I sat there seven days appalled in their midst.

en.L: And I came to the exiles at Tel-abib, who were living by the river Kebar, and I sat where they were living, and I sat there seven days, appalled, among them.
en.B: I came to the exiles at Tel-abib, who lived by the Kebar Canal. I sat where they were living, and for seven days I sat among them, stunned.
en.R: I came to the exiles at Tel-abib, who lived by the Kebar Canal. For seven days I sat there among them, deeply shocked.

pt.L: E cheguei aos exilados em Tel-Abibe, que moravam junto ao rio Quebar, e me sentei onde eles moravam, e fiquei sentado ali sete dias, atônito, no meio deles.
pt.B: Cheguei aos exilados em Tel-Abibe, que moravam à beira do canal Quebar. Sentei-me onde eles moravam, e por sete dias fiquei sentado entre eles, atordoado.
pt.R: Cheguei aos exilados em Tel-Abibe, que moravam perto do canal Quebar. Durante sete dias fiquei sentado ali com eles, profundamente chocado.

decisions.choice: and I sat: the reading tradition, against the written form
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text read differently here (as "and which"), but the scribes' marginal note says to read "and I sat", which fits the rest of the verse. The marginal reading is followed.

decisions.choice: Tel-abib: a settlement of the exiles
decisions.reason: A "tel" is a mound of ruins left by an old town. The name is the Babylonian "mound of the flood", an old ruined site, taken up into Hebrew as "hill of grain". The exiles were settled at such abandoned sites to rebuild and farm them. The modern city of Tel Aviv took its name from this verse.

decisions.choice: appalled: stunned into silence
decisions.reason: The word means desolate, appalled, struck dumb with horror. Seven days is the time of mourning for the dead (Genesis 50:10; Job 2:13, where Job's friends sit with him seven days without speaking). Ezekiel sits with the people in silence before his first message comes (verse 16).

decisions.choice: the Kebar Canal (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:1. Readable leaves out the clause "I sat where they were living", which the next words repeat.

decisions.choice: Tel-Abibe
decisions.reason: The settlement (m2) takes the usual Brazilian form, with the final vowel Portuguese adds after a consonant and a capital on each part, as the shared rules for Ezekiel set it. "Tel Aviv", the modern city named after it, is left to the meaning note.

source.text: וַיְהִ֕י מִקְצֵ֖ה שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑יםפוַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was at [the] end of seven days, and came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:

en.L: And it came about at the end of seven days, and the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:
en.B: After the seven days were over, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:
en.R: When the seven days were over, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

pt.L: E aconteceu, ao fim de sete dias, que a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio a mim, dizendo:
pt.B: Passados os sete dias, a palavra {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio a mim:
pt.R: Quando os sete dias terminaram, {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} me deu esta mensagem:

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to me, saying: a new message begins
decisions.reason: This is the book's usual heading for a message from the LORD; it occurs about fifty times. It marks a new section, here after the seven days of silence.

decisions.choice: The word of the LORD came to me, saying: (L); the word of the LORD came to me: (B); the LORD gave me this message: (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula in Jeremiah and used throughout Ezekiel.

decisions.choice: E a palavra do SENHOR veio a mim, dizendo: (L); A palavra do SENHOR veio a mim: (B); O SENHOR me deu esta mensagem: (R)
alternatives: Veio a mim a palavra do SENHOR
decisions.reason: For the whole book (about fifty times, m1): the heading of a new message keeps the wording Jeremiah 1:4 sets in Portuguese at each level, as the English does (r-en-1). Literal keeps "dizendo:"; Balanced introduces the message with the colon alone; Readable says that the LORD gave the message.

source.text: בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם צֹפֶ֥ה נְתַתִּ֖יךָ לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְשָׁמַעְתָּ֤ מִפִּי֙ דָּבָ֔ר וְהִזְהַרְתָּ֥ אוֹתָ֖ם מִמֶּֽנִּי׃

records.literal_gloss: Son of man, a watchman I have made you for [the] house of Israel; and you will hear from my mouth a word and warn them from me.

en.L: Son of man, a watchman I have made you for the house of Israel; and you will hear a word from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mouth and warn them from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: Son of man, I have appointed you a watchman for the house of Israel. When you hear a word from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mouth, you must warn them for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the people of Israel. Whenever you hear a message from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, you must warn them for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

pt.L: Filho do homem, eu te pus [como] sentinela para a casa de Israel; e ouvirás da {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} boca uma palavra e os advertirás da {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} parte.
pt.B: Filho do homem, eu te designei sentinela para a casa de Israel. Quando ouvires uma palavra da {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} boca, deves adverti-los da {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} parte.
pt.R: Filho do homem, eu te fiz sentinela para o povo de Israel. Sempre que ouvires uma mensagem {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}}, deves avisá-los da {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} parte.

decisions.choice: a watchman: a lookout who warns the city of danger
decisions.reason: A watchman stood on the city wall or a tower and called out when he saw an enemy coming, so that the people could prepare (2 Samuel 18:24-27; 2 Kings 9:17-20). The prophets are called watchmen (Isaiah 56:10; Jeremiah 6:17; Hosea 9:8). Ezekiel's task is to warn each person of the danger they are in. The charge is given again, in almost the same words, at the fall of Jerusalem (33:1-9).

decisions.choice: warn them from me: the warning comes from the LORD himself
decisions.reason: The danger the watchman sees is the LORD's own judgment, and the warning is also from the LORD. The one who brings the judgment sends the warning so that people may turn and live (18:23, 32).

decisions.choice: watchman (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: "Watchman" is kept at every level; it is the picture the whole passage turns on. The message that follows the heading of verse 16 is the LORD's oracle and takes no quotation marks, by the rule set for Ezekiel.

decisions.choice: sentinela (every level)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also 33:2-9): the lookout on the city wall (m1) is "sentinela" at every level, as the English keeps "watchman" (r-en-1). "Atalaia" is the old Bible word, now rare; "vigia" suggests a night guard of a building rather than a lookout who warns of an enemy.

source.text: בְּאָמְרִ֤י לָֽרָשָׁע֙ מ֣וֹת תָּמ֔וּת וְלֹ֣א הִזְהַרְתּ֗וֹ וְלֹ֥א דִבַּ֛רְתָּ לְהַזְהִ֥יר רָשָׁ֛ע מִדַּרְכּ֥וֹ הָרְשָׁעָ֖ה לְחַיֹּת֑וֹ ה֤וּא רָשָׁע֙ בַּעֲוֺנ֣וֹ יָמ֔וּת וְדָמ֖וֹ מִיָּדְךָ֥ אֲבַקֵּֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: When I say to [the] wicked, Surely you will die, and you do not warn him and do not speak to warn [the] wicked from his way the wicked to keep him alive, he, [the] wicked, in his iniquity will die, and his blood from your hand I will require.

en.L: When I say to the wicked, "You will surely die," and you do not warn {{gender:them|him}}, and do not speak to warn the wicked from {{gender:their|his}} wicked way to keep {{gender:them|him}} alive, that wicked [person] will die for {{gender:their|his}} iniquity, but {{gender:their|his}} blood I will require from your hand.
en.B: If I say to a wicked person, "You will surely die," and you do not warn {{gender:them|him}} or speak out to turn {{gender:them|him}} from {{gender:their|his}} wicked way and save {{gender:their|his}} life, that wicked person will die for {{gender:their|his}} sin, but I will hold you responsible for {{gender:their|his}} death.
en.R: Suppose I tell a wicked person, "You will certainly die." If you do not warn {{gender:them|him}} to turn from {{gender:their|his}} evil ways so that {{gender:they|he}} can live, that wicked person will die because of {{gender:their|his}} sin. But I will hold you responsible for {{gender:their|his}} death.

pt.L: Quando eu disser ao ímpio: "Certamente morrerás", e tu não o advertires, e não falares para advertir o ímpio do seu caminho perverso, para conservá-lo vivo, esse ímpio morrerá pela sua iniquidade, mas o sangue dele eu requererei da tua mão.
pt.B: Se eu disser a um ímpio: "Certamente morrerás", e tu não o advertires nem falares para desviá-lo do seu caminho perverso e salvar a sua vida, esse ímpio morrerá pelo seu pecado, mas eu te considerarei responsável pela morte dele.
pt.R: Imagina que eu diga a uma pessoa má: "Tu vais morrer, com certeza." Se tu não a avisares para deixar os seus maus caminhos e assim continuar viva, essa pessoa má vai morrer por causa do seu pecado. Mas eu vou te considerar responsável pela morte dela.

decisions.choice: his blood I will require from your hand: I will hold you responsible for his death
decisions.reason: To require someone's blood is to call them to account for a death, as for a murder (Genesis 9:5; 2 Samuel 4:11). A watchman who sees the danger and keeps silent shares the guilt for the deaths that follow.

decisions.choice: you will surely die: death in the coming judgment
decisions.reason: The doubled verb is the form of a death sentence (Genesis 2:17; 1 Kings 2:37). Here it is the death that the coming judgment will bring: the sword, famine and plague of chapters 5-7. The passage, like chapters 18 and 33, is about life and death for each person in that judgment, and it does not set out a teaching about life after death.

decisions.choice: the wicked will die for his iniquity: each person answers for their own wrong
decisions.reason: The wicked person is not excused because no one warned them; they die for their own sin. Ezekiel 18 sets out this teaching at length. The watchman, too, answers for what he does with the warning.

decisions.choice: them, their / him, his (gender setting)
decisions.reason: The wicked person here stands for anyone, man or woman, so the pronouns take the gender setting, with the traditional "him" and "his" as the alternative. *'Awon* is "iniquity" at Literal and "sin" at Balanced and Readable, as in Isaiah. Balanced and Readable say "hold you responsible" for the idiom in m1.

decisions.choice: o ímpio, o justo ... ele (L, B); uma pessoa má, uma pessoa justa ... ela (R); no gender setting
decisions.reason: For the whole book (3:18-21; 18; 33:7-20): the English puts the pronouns for the wicked and the righteous under the gender setting. Portuguese "o ímpio" and "o justo" are generic, meaning anyone, and the "ele" that refers back to them is ordinary generic Portuguese (style section 7), so Literal and Balanced need no setting; Readable says "uma pessoa má" and "uma pessoa justa", and its pronouns agree with "pessoa". Tsedaqah is "retidão" at Literal and Balanced, as Isaiah 1:21 sets it.

source.text: וְאַתָּה֙ כִּֽי־הִזְהַ֣רְתָּ רָשָׁ֔ע וְלֹא־שָׁב֙ מֵֽרִשְׁע֔וֹ וּמִדַּרְכּ֖וֹ הָרְשָׁעָ֑ה ה֚וּא בַּעֲוֺנ֣וֹ יָמ֔וּת וְאַתָּ֖ה אֶֽת־נַפְשְׁךָ֥ הִצַּֽלְתָּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And you, if you warn [the] wicked, and he does not turn from his wickedness and from his way the wicked, he in his iniquity will die, and you your soul have delivered.

en.L: But you, if you warn the wicked, and {{gender:they do|he does}} not turn from {{gender:their|his}} wickedness and from {{gender:their|his}} wicked way, {{gender:they|he}} will die for {{gender:their|his}} iniquity, but you will have delivered your life.
en.B: But if you warn the wicked and {{gender:they do|he does}} not turn from {{gender:their|his}} wickedness or {{gender:their|his}} wicked way, {{gender:they|he}} will die for {{gender:their|his}} sin, but you will have saved yourself.
en.R: But suppose you warn the wicked person, and {{gender:they do|he does}} not turn away from {{gender:their|his}} evil ways. Then {{gender:they|he}} will die because of {{gender:their|his}} sin, but you will have saved your own life.

pt.L: Mas tu, se advertires o ímpio, e ele não se afastar da sua impiedade e do seu caminho perverso, ele morrerá pela sua iniquidade, mas tu terás livrado a tua vida.
pt.B: Mas, se advertires o ímpio, e ele não se afastar da sua impiedade nem do seu caminho perverso, ele morrerá pelo seu pecado, mas tu terás salvado a tua própria vida.
pt.R: Mas imagina que avises a pessoa má, e ela não se afaste dos seus maus caminhos. Então ela vai morrer por causa do seu pecado, mas tu terás salvado a tua própria vida.

decisions.choice: you will have delivered your life: you will have saved yourself
decisions.reason: The word often translated "soul" here means the life or self of the person. The watchman who gives the warning is free of the guilt of verse 18, whatever the hearer does.

decisions.choice: they, their / he, his (gender setting)
decisions.reason: As in verse 18.

source.text: וּבְשׁ֨וּב צַדִּ֤יק מִצִּדְקוֹ֙ וְעָ֣שָׂה עָ֔וֶל וְנָתַתִּ֥י מִכְשׁ֛וֹל לְפָנָ֖יו ה֣וּא יָמ֑וּת כִּ֣י לֹ֤א הִזְהַרְתּוֹ֙ בְּחַטָּאת֣וֹ יָמ֔וּת וְלֹ֣א תִזָּכַ֗רְןָ צִדְקֹתָו֙אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה וְדָמ֖וֹ מִיָּדְךָ֥ אֲבַקֵּֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And when turns a righteous [one] from his righteousness and does injustice, and I put a stumbling block before him, he will die; because you did not warn him, in his sin he will die, and not will be remembered his righteous deeds which he did, and his blood from your hand I will require.

en.L: And when a righteous [person] turns from {{gender:their|his}} righteousness and does wrong, and I put a stumbling block before {{gender:them|him}}, {{gender:they|he}} will die. Because you did not warn {{gender:them|him}}, {{gender:they|he}} will die in {{gender:their|his}} sin, and {{gender:their|his}} righteous deeds that {{gender:they|he}} did will not be remembered; but {{gender:their|his}} blood I will require from your hand.
en.B: Again, if a righteous person turns away from {{gender:their|his}} righteousness and does wrong, and I lay a stumbling block before {{gender:them|him}}, {{gender:they|he}} will die. Since you did not warn {{gender:them|him}}, {{gender:they|he}} will die for {{gender:their|his}} sin, and the righteous things {{gender:they|he}} did will not be remembered. But I will hold you responsible for {{gender:their|his}} death.
en.R: Or suppose a righteous person stops doing what is right and does evil, and I put something in {{gender:their|his}} way to make {{gender:them|him}} fall. Then {{gender:they|he}} will die. If you did not warn {{gender:them|him}}, {{gender:they|he}} will die because of {{gender:their|his}} sin. The good things {{gender:they|he}} did before will not be remembered. But I will hold you responsible for {{gender:their|his}} death.

pt.L: E quando um justo se desviar da sua retidão e praticar o mal, e eu puser um tropeço diante dele, ele morrerá. Porque tu não o advertiste, ele morrerá no seu pecado, e os seus atos de retidão que ele praticou não serão lembrados; mas o sangue dele eu requererei da tua mão.
pt.B: Também, se um justo se desviar da sua retidão e praticar o mal, e eu puser uma pedra de tropeço diante dele, ele morrerá. Como tu não o advertiste, ele morrerá pelo seu pecado, e as coisas justas que ele fez não serão lembradas. Mas eu te considerarei responsável pela morte dele.
pt.R: Ou imagina que uma pessoa justa deixe de fazer o que é certo e faça o mal, e eu ponha alguma coisa no caminho dela para fazê-la cair. Então ela vai morrer. Se tu não a avisaste, ela vai morrer por causa do seu pecado. As coisas boas que ela fez antes não serão lembradas. Mas eu vou te considerar responsável pela morte dela.

decisions.choice: I put a stumbling block before him: the LORD brings the fall that follows the turning
decisions.reason: A stumbling block is something that trips a person and makes them fall. The person has already turned from what is right; the LORD then lets the consequence come, a trial or a disaster in which they fall. The same word is used for the people's idols and sins, "the stumbling block of their iniquity" (7:19; 14:3). The verse does not say that God leads a righteous person into sin.

decisions.choice: his righteous deeds will not be remembered: past goodness does not cancel present wrong
decisions.reason: Ezekiel 18:24 and 33:12-13 say the same: a person is judged by the way they are living, not by what they once did. The plural "righteousnesses" means righteous deeds.

decisions.choice: they, their / he, his (gender setting)
decisions.reason: As in verse 18. *Tsedaqah* is "righteousness" at Literal and Balanced; Readable says "stops doing what is right" and "the good things they did", and "something in their way to make them fall" for the stumbling block (m1).

source.text: וְאַתָּ֞ה כִּ֧י הִזְהַרְתּ֣וֹ צַדִּ֗יק לְבִלְתִּ֥י חֲטֹ֛א צַדִּ֖יק וְה֣וּא לֹא־חָטָ֑א חָי֤וֹ יִֽחְיֶה֙ כִּ֣י נִזְהָ֔ר וְאַתָּ֖ה אֶֽת־נַפְשְׁךָ֥ הִצַּֽלְתָּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And you, if you have warned him, [the] righteous, not to sin, [the] righteous, and he does not sin, surely he will live, because he was warned, and you your soul have delivered.

en.L: But you, if you warn the righteous not to sin, and {{gender:they do|he does}} not sin, {{gender:they|he}} will surely live, because {{gender:they|he}} took warning; and you will have delivered your life.
en.B: But if you warn the righteous person not to sin, and {{gender:they do|he does}} not sin, {{gender:they|he}} will certainly live, because {{gender:they|he}} took the warning, and you will have saved yourself.
en.R: But suppose you warn the righteous person not to sin, and {{gender:they do|he does}} not sin. Then {{gender:they|he}} will certainly live because {{gender:they|he}} listened to your warning. And you will have saved your own life.

pt.L: Mas tu, se advertires o justo para que o justo não peque, e ele não pecar, certamente viverá, porque foi advertido; e tu terás livrado a tua vida.
pt.B: Mas, se advertires o justo para que não peque, e ele não pecar, ele certamente viverá, porque aceitou a advertência, e tu terás salvado a tua própria vida.
pt.R: Mas imagina que avises a pessoa justa para não pecar, e ela não peque. Então ela certamente vai viver, porque escutou o teu aviso. E tu terás salvado a tua própria vida.

decisions.choice: if you warn him, the righteous, not to sin: the fourth case
decisions.reason: The passage sets out four cases: the wicked unwarned (verse 18), the wicked warned (verse 19), the righteous unwarned (verse 20) and the righteous warned (here). The Hebrew names "the righteous" twice, awkwardly; the sense is plain.

decisions.choice: he will surely live: the promise of chapters 18 and 33
decisions.reason: "He will surely live" is the verdict given to the righteous in 18:9 and 33:13-16. The watchman's warning can save a life.

decisions.choice: they / he (gender setting)
decisions.reason: As in verse 18.

source.text: וַתְּהִ֥י עָלַ֛י שָׁ֖ם יַד־יְהוָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י ק֥וּם צֵא֙ אֶל־הַבִּקְעָ֔ה וְשָׁ֖ם אֲדַבֵּ֥ר אוֹתָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And was on me there [the] hand of Yahweh, and he said to me, Arise, go out to the valley, and there I will speak with you.

en.L: And the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was upon me there, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Arise, go out to the valley, and there I will speak with you."
en.B: There the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came on me, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Get up and go out into the valley, and there I will speak with you."
en.R: There the power of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came on me, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to me, "Get up and go out to the valley. I will speak to you there."

pt.L: E a mão {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} estava sobre mim ali, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me disse: "Levanta-te, sai para o vale, e ali falarei contigo."
pt.B: Ali a mão {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio sobre mim, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me disse: "Levanta-te e sai para o vale, e ali falarei contigo."
pt.R: Ali o poder {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} veio sobre mim, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} me disse: "Levanta-te e vai até o vale. Ali eu vou falar contigo."

decisions.choice: the valley: a broad, open plain
decisions.reason: The word means a wide valley or plain between hills. It is the same place, or the same kind of place, as the valley of dry bones in 37:1, and the plain where Ezekiel saw the glory in 8:4.

decisions.choice: the hand of the LORD was upon me (L); came on me (B); the power of the LORD came on me (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula in Ezekiel (see 1:3).

source.text: וָאָקוּם֮ וָאֵצֵ֣א אֶל־הַבִּקְעָה֒ וְהִנֵּה־שָׁ֤ם כְּבוֹד־יְהוָה֙ עֹמֵ֔ד כַּכָּב֕וֹד אֲשֶׁ֥ר רָאִ֖יתִי עַל־נְהַר־כְּבָ֑ר וָאֶפֹּ֖ל עַל־פָּנָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And I arose and went out to the valley, and see, there [the] glory of Yahweh [was] standing, like the glory which I had seen by [the] river Kebar, and I fell on my face.

en.L: And I arose and went out to the valley, and see, the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was standing there, like the glory that I had seen by the river Kebar, and I fell on my face.
en.B: So I got up and went out into the valley, and there stood the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, like the glory I had seen by the Kebar Canal, and I fell face down.
en.R: So I got up and went out to the valley. The glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was there, just like the glory I had seen by the Kebar Canal. I bowed down with my face to the ground.

pt.L: E me levantei e saí para o vale, e eis que a glória {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} estava ali, como a glória que eu tinha visto junto ao rio Quebar, e caí sobre o meu rosto.
pt.B: Então me levantei e saí para o vale, e ali estava a glória {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, como a glória que eu tinha visto à beira do canal Quebar, e caí com o rosto em terra.
pt.R: Então me levantei e fui até o vale. A glória {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}} estava ali, igual à glória que eu tinha visto perto do canal Quebar. Eu me curvei com o rosto no chão.

decisions.choice: like the glory I had seen by the river Kebar: the vision of chapter 1
decisions.reason: Ezekiel sees again the glory of chapter 1 (1:28), and responds as he did then, falling on his face. The glory will appear to him again in the temple (8:4) and leaving it (10:18; 11:23).

decisions.choice: fell face down (B); bowed down with my face to the ground (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:28.

records.literal_gloss: And came into me a spirit, and it set me on my feet, and he spoke with me and said to me, Go, be shut in inside your house.

en.L: And [the] Spirit came into me and made me stand on my feet, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke with me and said to me, "Go, be shut in inside your house.
en.B: Then the Spirit came into me and set me on my feet, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke with me and said, "Go and shut yourself inside your house.
en.R: Then the Spirit came into me and made me stand up. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to me and said, "Go home and shut yourself inside your house.

pt.L: E [o] Espírito entrou em mim e me pôs de pé sobre os meus pés, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} falou comigo e me disse: "Vai, encerra-te dentro da tua casa.
pt.B: Então o Espírito entrou em mim e me pôs de pé, e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} falou comigo e disse: "Vai e tranca-te dentro da tua casa.
pt.R: Então o Espírito entrou em mim e me fez ficar de pé. {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} falou comigo e disse: "Vai para casa e tranca-te lá dentro.

decisions.choice: the Spirit ... he: the Spirit raises him, the LORD speaks
decisions.reason: As in 2:2, the Spirit enters Ezekiel and sets him on his feet. "He" who speaks is the LORD, the speaker throughout these chapters.

decisions.choice: shut yourself inside your house: Ezekiel is to withdraw from public life
decisions.reason: The command, with verses 25-26, keeps Ezekiel from going about among the people as an ordinary prophet would. It does not stop him from acting out the signs of chapters 4-5 in the sight of the people, or the elders from visiting him at home (8:1; 14:1; 20:1). The text does not say how long the confinement lasted.

decisions.choice: The LORD spoke to me (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the LORD for "he", since the Spirit was just mentioned and a reader might take "he" to mean the Spirit (m1). The speech runs to the end of verse 27.

source.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־אָדָ֗ם הִנֵּ֨ה נָתְנ֤וּ עָלֶ֨יךָ֙ עֲבוֹתִ֔ים וַאֲסָר֖וּךָ בָּהֶ֑ם וְלֹ֥א תֵצֵ֖א בְּתוֹכָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, son of man, see, they will put on you ropes and bind you with them, and not you will go out in their midst.

en.L: And you, son of man, see, they will put cords on you and bind you with them, and you will not go out in their midst.
en.B: As for you, son of man, ropes will be put on you, and you will be tied up with them, so that you cannot go out among the people.
en.R: Son of man, you will be tied up with ropes, so that you cannot go out among the people.

pt.L: E tu, filho do homem, eis que porão cordas sobre ti e te amarrarão com elas, e não sairás para o meio deles.
pt.B: Quanto a ti, filho do homem, cordas serão postas em ti, e serás amarrado com elas, de modo que não poderás sair para o meio do povo.
pt.R: Filho do homem, tu serás amarrado com cordas e não vais poder sair para o meio do povo.

decisions.choice: they will put cords on you: you will be bound
alternatives: the people will tie you up
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject. It may be the people who bind Ezekiel, to stop him speaking among them, or it may be an impersonal "cords will be put on you". In 4:8 the LORD himself says, "I will put cords on you". Whether the cords were real or a figure for the restraint God places on him is not said.

decisions.choice: ropes will be put on you (B); you will be tied up (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the passive, which leaves the subject open as the Hebrew does (m1). Balanced and Readable name "the people" for "them".

source.text: וּלְשֽׁוֹנְךָ֙ אַדְבִּ֣יק אֶל־חִכֶּ֔ךָ וְנֶֽאֱלַ֔מְתָּ וְלֹא־תִֽהְיֶ֥ה לָהֶ֖ם לְאִ֣ישׁ מוֹכִ֑יחַ כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And your tongue I will make cling to your palate, and you will be mute, and not you will be to them a man reproving, for a house of rebellion [are] they.

en.L: And I will make your tongue cling to the roof of your mouth, and you will be mute and will not be to them a man who rebukes, for they [are] a house of rebellion.
en.B: I will make your tongue cling to the roof of your mouth, so that you will be silent and unable to rebuke them, for they are a rebellious house.
en.R: I will make your tongue stick fast to the roof of your mouth, so that you cannot speak. You will not be able to correct them, because they are people who refuse to obey.

pt.L: E farei a tua língua se pegar ao céu da tua boca, e ficarás mudo e não serás para eles um homem que repreende, pois eles [são] uma casa de rebelião.
pt.B: Farei a tua língua se prender ao céu da boca, de modo que ficarás calado e não poderás repreendê-los, pois são uma casa rebelde.
pt.R: Vou fazer a tua língua grudar no céu da boca, e tu não vais conseguir falar. Não vais poder corrigi-los, porque eles são um povo que se recusa a obedecer.

decisions.choice: you will be mute and will not be a man who rebukes: Ezekiel will speak only when the LORD speaks
alternatives: a complete loss of speech for a time
decisions.reason: Ezekiel goes on speaking the LORD's messages through chapters 4-24, so his silence is not total. Verse 27 explains it: he will open his mouth only when the LORD gives him a word, and will not speak to the people on his own as one who argues and pleads with them. The silence ends when news comes that Jerusalem has fallen (24:25-27; 33:21-22).

decisions.choice: a man who rebukes: one who reproves, or one who pleads a case
decisions.reason: The word means to rebuke or set right, and also to argue a case or to judge between two parties (Job 9:33, "an arbiter"). Ezekiel will not be able to plead with the people, or for them.

decisions.choice: a house of rebellion / a rebellious house / people who refuse to obey
decisions.reason: The wording set at 2:5.

source.text: וּֽבְדַבְּרִ֤י אֽוֹתְךָ֙ אֶפְתַּ֣ח אֶת־פִּ֔יךָ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֑ה הַשֹּׁמֵ֤עַ׀יִשְׁמָע֙ וְהֶחָדֵ֣ל׀יֶחְדָּ֔ל כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵֽמָּה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And when I speak with you I will open your mouth, and you will say to them, Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: the one hearing, let him hear, and the one refraining, let him refrain, for a house of rebellion [are] they.

en.L: And at my speaking with you, I will open your mouth, and you will say to them, Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}. Whoever hears, let {{gender:them|him}} hear; and whoever refrains, let {{gender:them|him}} refrain; for they [are] a house of rebellion."
en.B: Whenever I speak with you, I will open your mouth, and you will say to them, The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this. Whoever will listen, let {{gender:them|him}} listen, and whoever refuses, let {{gender:them|him}} refuse, for they are a rebellious house."
en.R: But when I have a message for you, I will open your mouth. Then you will tell them, This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says. Anyone who wants to listen may listen, and anyone who refuses may refuse. They are people who refuse to obey."

pt.L: E quando eu falar contigo, abrirei a tua boca, e tu lhes dirás: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}. Quem ouve, ouça; e quem deixa de ouvir, deixe de ouvir; pois eles [são] uma casa de rebelião."
pt.B: Sempre que eu falar contigo, abrirei a tua boca, e tu lhes dirás: Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}}. Quem quiser escutar, que escute; e quem se recusar, que se recuse; pois são uma casa rebelde."
pt.R: Mas, quando eu tiver uma mensagem para ti, abrirei a tua boca. Então dirás a eles: É isto que o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} diz. Quem quiser escutar pode escutar, e quem se recusar pode se recusar. Eles são um povo que se recusa a obedecer."

decisions.choice: whoever hears, let him hear: the LORD's words to Ezekiel
decisions.reason: The words after the formula can be read as part of what Ezekiel is to say, or as the LORD's comment to him. Taken as the LORD's comment, they close the commission with the same thought as 2:5 and 2:7: the prophet speaks; the hearers choose.

decisions.choice: whoever hears, let him hear: "He who has ears, let him hear"
decisions.reason: Jesus ends his parables with "He who has ears to hear, let him hear" (Matthew 11:15; 13:9), and the risen Christ ends each letter of Revelation 2-3 with "Whoever has an ear, let him hear". The saying leaves the hearer responsible for their own response.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD / The Lord GOD says this / This is what the Lord GOD says
decisions.reason: The formula as set at 2:4; the message Ezekiel is to deliver takes no quotation marks of its own. The verbs "hear" and "refrain" follow the wording of 2:5 at each level. The listener stands for anyone, so the pronouns take the gender setting. The quotation mark closes the speech begun in verse 24.

decisions.choice: Quem ouve, ouça (L); Quem quiser escutar, que escute (B); quem ... pode (R); no gender setting
alternatives: Aquele que ouve, que ele ouça
decisions.reason: "Quem" already means anyone, man or woman, so Portuguese needs no pronoun and no gender setting where the English has "let them hear" (style section 7). Literal says "Quem ouve, ouça", the shape of the Gospels' "Quem tem ouvidos, ouça", which this saying anticipates (m2).
